question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mfenced></math> on treatment with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Br</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>FeBr</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CCl</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> produced a single isomer <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>8</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>Br</mi></math> wile heating <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mfenced></math> with sodalime gives toluene. The compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open="["><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mfenced></math> is:

solution.text:
Isomer C8H7O2Br on heating with sodalime gives toluene,hence it is an acid.Moreover since it has Degree of unsaturation 5 therefore it is an aromatic carboxylic acid.Since Carboxylic acid on heating gives toluene ,therefore it is having -CH3 group attached to the benzene ring.

Now it forms single isomer on halogenation, therefore -CH3 group must be attached at para position with respect to -COOH group.

Hence correct option is 1.
